clue.text: Celestial origins of big bang?

parts.note: the 'big bang' is not the start of the universe but a loud crash of thunder, whose source is up in the sky

explanation.walkthrough: 'Big bang' and 'Celestial origins' point to cosmology; the bang is a thunderclap, and its origins in the sky are the clouds that produce it.
explanation.definitionFit: Storm masses in the sky are where the crash of thunder comes from, so they are the heavenly source of a loud bang.

clue.text: Bull may suffer during this

parts.note: the bull is not an animal but the bull's-eye at the centre of a dartboard or archery target, hit repeatedly in training

explanation.walkthrough: The bull suggests an animal enduring something; it is the bull's-eye, which takes the punishment when people practise their aim.
explanation.definitionFit: Shooting or archery training means firing repeatedly at a board whose centre is called the bull.

clue.text: Final warning from Tim, and mutual jostling

indicators.note: jostling pushes things about, so the letters of the two words are pushed into a new order

explanation.surface: Tim and another person shove each other until one issues a last warning.
explanation.walkthrough: 'jostling' rearranges TIM and MUTUAL together; 'and' only joins the two fodder words, and 'from' links the wordplay to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: An ultimatum is a last demand backed by a threat, a final warning before action.

clue.text: No light in deckhouse initially, and boat by headland

indicators.note: initially points to the opening letter of the word deckhouse

parts.note: Noah's ark is a boat
a ness is a headland, as in Scottish place names like Loch Ness's neighbours and Dungeness

explanation.surface: A ship's deckhouse is unlit, and a boat sits beside a promontory.
explanation.walkthrough: 'by' just places the pieces next to each other: D from 'deckhouse initially', then ARK, then NESS.
explanation.definitionFit: Darkness is the absence of illumination, the state where there is nothing to see by.

clue.text: Drops rule, one hears

indicators.note: one hears signals that the word for rule is spoken and a word sounding the same is entered

parts.note: a monarch's reign is their rule

explanation.surface: A ruling is abandoned, as someone reports.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Drops' looks like a verb; it is the noun, falling drops of water.
explanation.definitionFit: Precipitation falls as water droplets, so drops from the sky are what we call a shower.

clue.text: Heather having disturbed night, it strikes one

indicators.note: having means holding, so the word for heather holds the other piece inside it

parts.note: ling is another name for heather

indicators.note: disturbed means stirred up, so the letters of night are jumbled

explanation.surface: Heather endures a restless night, and something comes to her as a sudden realisation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Heather' reads as a woman's name but is the plant LING; 'disturbed' turns NIGHT into GHTNI, which 'having' places inside LING.
explanation.definitionFit: A bolt from a storm hits a person or tree, so it is the thing that strikes someone.

clue.text: Part coming up in Verdi, as Nubian? Not mentioned

indicators.note: coming up in a down entry means the letters are read from bottom to top, backwards
Part means only a portion of the following words is used, a run of consecutive letters

explanation.surface: A role in a Verdi opera is sung by a Nubian, as in Aida.
explanation.walkthrough: The run DIASNU sits across 'verDI AS NUbian'; 'coming up' reverses it, as this is a down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Something left unspoken is not mentioned; nobody voiced it.

clue.text: Smooth patch

definitions.meaning: glossy and smooth, or smoothly persuasive
a patch of oil spreading on water

explanation.definitionFit: Slick describes a glossy, slippery surface, and as a noun is a film or stain of oil floating on the sea.

clue.text: Caption on Durer strangely not included

indicators.note: strangely means in an odd way, so the letters of the three words are put into an odd new order

explanation.surface: A label on a Dürer print has been left out of the catalogue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'strangely' rearranges all fourteen letters of CAPTION ON DURER.
explanation.definitionFit: Unincorporated means not formed into or made part of a larger body, so left out.

clue.text: It provides lift each way

indicators.note: each way says the word reads the same in both directions, forwards and backwards

parts.note: these definition words give the whole answer, and the answer is itself the palindrome: it reads the same from either end

explanation.surface: A lift that works in both directions, up and down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'each way' suggests a betting term or a two-way lift; it says the answer reads the same in either direction.
explanation.definitionFit: A helicopter's spinning blades form the rotor, which gives the craft its upward force.

clue.text: Dyspepsia — Di avoided eating

indicators.note: avoided means kept away from, so the name Di is left out of the longer word

parts.note: dyspepsia is the medical term for indigestion
Di is taken as the letters D and I

explanation.surface: Di has an upset stomach, so she skipped her meal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'avoided' removes DI from INDIGESTION, leaving a word for the taking in of food.
explanation.definitionFit: Ingestion is the act of taking food into the body, swallowing a meal.

clue.text: Queen has hole in fur

parts.note: ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the abbreviation for the Queen
a mine is a hole dug in the ground

explanation.surface: The Queen's fur coat has a hole in it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'has' only joins ER and MINE; 'hole in fur' suggests a tear in a coat.
explanation.definitionFit: Ermine is the white winter pelt of the stoat, used to trim royal robes.

clue.text: Badly hit, wrench gun around

indicators.note: around means the gun word goes round the wrench word, enclosing it

parts.note: the Sten is a British submachine gun
to rick a joint is to wrench or sprain it

explanation.surface: Someone badly hurt twists a gun round in their hand.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wrench' looks like a tool or a noun; it is the verb RICK, to sprain, which goes inside STEN.
explanation.definitionFit: Stricken means badly affected or struck down, as by illness or misfortune.

clue.text: Fancy pastries — i.e. here?

indicators.note: Fancy here works as a verb-like signal meaning made elaborate, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Elaborate cakes, that is, the kind sold in this shop.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fancy pastries' reads as the definition, but 'Fancy' rearranges PASTRIES plus IE; 'here?' is the definition, the place where such cakes are sold.
explanation.definitionFit: A patisserie is a cake shop, the place where such sweet baked goods are made and sold.

clue.text: Moves abroad -it's good in Arab states

indicators.note: in places the abbreviation for good inside the word for the Arab states

parts.note: the Emirates are the Arab states of the UAE

explanation.surface: Someone relocates overseas, finding life pleasant in the Gulf.
explanation.walkthrough: 'it's' is a link; G goes into EMIRATES.
explanation.definitionFit: To emigrate is to leave one's country to settle in another, to relocate overseas.

clue.text: Three things to put round centre of atrium

indicators.note: put round means the word to is placed around the other piece, enclosing it
centre of picks the two middle letters of the six-letter word atrium

explanation.surface: Three objects are to be arranged around the middle of a hall.
explanation.walkthrough: The centre of the six letters of ATRIUM is RI, which TO surrounds.
explanation.definitionFit: A trio is a set of three, a group of three items or people.

clue.text: Selects new cardinals?

parts.note: the cardinals are not churchmen chosen by a pope but cardinal numbers, assigned afresh

explanation.walkthrough: Cardinals suggests the Vatican; cardinal numbers are one, two, three, so giving things new ones is reassigning their numbers.
explanation.definitionFit: To give items fresh numerals in sequence is to assign new cardinal numbers to them.

clue.text: Spat chewed stuff in a hole

indicators.note: in places the chewed stuff inside the phrase for a hole

parts.note: a rent is a tear or hole in fabric
gum is the stuff that gets chewed

explanation.surface: Someone spat out chewing gum into a hole.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spat' looks like the past of spit; it is a noun, a quarrel. GUM goes inside A RENT.
explanation.definitionFit: A spat is a petty quarrel, a disagreement or row.

clue.text: Soldiers run into woman

indicators.note: into places the abbreviation for run inside the woman's name

parts.note: Amy is a woman's name
R is the cricket abbreviation for run

explanation.surface: Troops charge at a woman.
explanation.walkthrough: R goes into AMY.
explanation.definitionFit: An army is a large body of troops organised for land warfare.

clue.text: Tough cookie: criticises chap returning after a drink

indicators.note: after places the reversed pieces following the drink

parts.note: gin is a drink

indicators.note: returning means the two words that come before it are read backwards

parts.note: pans means criticises harshly, as a reviewer does
Reg is a man's name, standing for any chap

explanation.surface: A hard person insults a man and then goes back to the bar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tough cookie' sounds like a resilient person; it is a crisp biscuit. 'returning' turns PANS and REG into GER SNAP, placed after GIN.
explanation.definitionFit: A gingersnap is a hard, crisp biscuit flavoured with ginger; cookie is the US word for biscuit.

clue.text: Period of play for 25 making illegal deliveries, say

indicators.note: say signals that the word is spoken and a word sounding like it is entered

parts.note: 25 refers to the clue at 25 across; a bowler in cricket who throws instead of bowling, an illegal delivery, is called a chucker

explanation.surface: A cricketer bowling illegally is given a spell of play.
explanation.walkthrough: '25' points to the answer at 25-across, a cricket player. In cricket the ball must be bowled with a straight arm; one who throws it is a chucker.
explanation.definitionFit: A chukka is one of the timed periods into which a polo match is divided.

clue.text: Garment supports one, right after hospital

indicators.note: after places the pieces for one and right following the hospital abbreviation

parts.note: in golf, tees support the ball before it is struck
H is the abbreviation for hospital, as on road signs
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Clothing holds someone up as they leave hospital in good shape.
explanation.walkthrough: 'supports' looks like a verb; it is a plural noun, golf tees.
explanation.definitionFit: A tee shirt is a collarless short-sleeved top, an item of casual clothing.

clue.text: Girl, in US, taking morning off

indicators.note: taking with off means the morning abbreviation is removed from the country
off with taking signals the removal of letters from the longer word

parts.note: the US is America
AM stands for morning, ante meridiem

explanation.surface: A girl in the United States skips her morning.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' is a link: AM is taken off AMERICA.
explanation.definitionFit: Erica is a girl's name.

clue.text: Bird in distant, German city

indicators.note: in places the German city inside the word for distant

parts.note: far means distant
Ulm is a city in southern Germany, on the Danube

explanation.surface: A bird is spotted in a faraway German city.
explanation.walkthrough: ULM goes inside FAR.
explanation.definitionFit: The fulmar is a grey and white seabird related to the petrels.

clue.text: Heck! Road not even, twisted instep

indicators.note: twisted means turned round, so the picked letters are read backwards
not even means the odd-numbered letters, first, third and so on, of the words are taken

explanation.surface: Someone curses an uneven road that twisted their foot.
explanation.walkthrough: The odd letters of HECK ROAD are H, C, R, A; 'twisted' reverses them.
explanation.definitionFit: The arch is the raised curve of the foot's sole, the part over the instep.

clue.text: Covers his situation, perhaps

parts.note: cover is a fielding position in cricket, so cover could be where a fielder is placed

explanation.walkthrough: 'Covers' looks like a verb about concealing; cover (or cover point) is a fielding position in cricket, the place where a player may be stationed.
explanation.definitionFit: A fielder in the bat-and-ball game may be stationed at the position called cover.

clue.text: Happening to be in flat with temperature

parts.note: even means flat, level

explanation.surface: Something occurs in a level place where it is warm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to be in' and 'with' are link words; EVEN is followed by T.
explanation.definitionFit: An event is an occurrence, something that takes place.

clue.text: At seaside then slipping, knocked out

indicators.note: slipping means sliding out of place, so the letters of the three words shift into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone at the seaside slips and is knocked unconscious.
explanation.walkthrough: 'slipping' rearranges AT SEASIDE THEN.
explanation.definitionFit: To be anaesthetised is to be made unconscious with drugs before surgery.
